music-scale.context: Four beamed notes stepping upward, the shape of a rising scale. Use it for scale practice, music theory lessons and ear training.

music-chord.context: Three note heads stacked on a single stem with a small flag, meaning notes played together. Use it for chords, harmony and piano or guitar lessons.

double-whole-note.context: An open oval note head flanked by a vertical bar on each side, the breve of written music. Use it for note value charts and notation lessons.

measure-repeat.context: A slanted slash with a dot on either side between two bar lines, the sign for repeating the previous measure. Use it in scores, charts and notation tools.

multi-measure-rest.context: A thick horizontal bar between two short end lines, the sign for several bars of silence in a row. Use it for orchestral parts and notation software.

chant-notation.context: A four-line staff with square note heads and a small clef at its start, in the style of medieval plainchant. Use it for sacred music, choirs and early music.

square-wave.context: A signal line that jumps between a high level and a low level with sharp right angles. Use it for synthesizer oscillators, pulse signals and electronics.

sawtooth-wave.context: A signal line of long rising ramps that each end in a sudden vertical drop. Use it for synthesizer waveforms, sound design and signal diagrams.

adsr-envelope.context: A shape that rises sharply, dips to a flat sustain level and then slopes down to zero, the classic synthesizer envelope. Use it for sound design controls.

crossfade.context: Two lines crossing in an X above a horizontal slider, one fading out as the other fades in. Use it for DJ mixing, audio editors and playlist transitions.

cardioid-pattern.context: A round polar plot with a heart-shaped pickup curve inside it, showing which directions a microphone hears best. Use it for microphone specs and recording guides.

spatial-audio.context: A head seen from the front with sound arcs curving around both sides. Use it for surround sound, head tracked audio and immersive listening settings.

music-recognition.context: A phone showing a music note with listening arcs beside it, the sign for identifying a song that is playing nearby. Use it for song identification features.

pitch-wheel.context: Two tall keyboard wheels side by side, one with a centre notch for pitch bend and one ridged for modulation. Use it for synthesizer and MIDI controller interfaces.

fingering-chart.context: The tube of a woodwind beside a column of open and filled finger holes. Use it for fingering guides, recorder and flute lessons and instrument tutorials.
